project.name: SASTRE DSL
project.description: A tool for creating clothing patterns using a domain-specific language, with geometric representation and SVG export
project.coordinate_system: Y-up internally (Cartesian), Y-down at SVG render via svgY = viewBoxHeight - internalY
project.build_order: vertical slices: each increment produces verifiable SVG
dsl_versions: v0.1: POINT/LINE/CURVE/PATH/EXPORT (no variables, no expressions, raw numbers = mm)

phases.description: Point, Segment (inline vector math), SVG Renderer, Export

phases.description: Vector, Line, Circle, Arc, Polygon, Transform, Measure (parallel to 02A)

phases.title: Intersections
phases.description: All intersection types decomposed, projections, tangents

phases.title: DSL v0.1 Minimal
phases.description: Lexer, Parser (no Pratt), Interpreter (no units), Model, Registry — no INPUT, no LET

phases.title: AI Kanban Operations
phases.description: Kanban Engine, CLI, Query API, Mutation API, Context Builder, OpenCode Skill for AI agents

tasks.description: Create src/kanban/engine/persistence.ts: KanbanPersistence (atomic write with temp file + rename), validateBeforeWrite (runs all validation checks), KanbanCache (in-memory cache with invalidation on write). acceptance_criteria: Atomic write: temp file + rename, no partial writes
Corrupted JSON handled gracefully with clear error
notes: Critical for data integrity
Uses PLAN-001 validator logic

tasks.title: Query API — getTask, getReadyTasks, getBlockedTasks, getTaskContext, getDependencies, getDependents, getChildren, getParent, getTree, getNextTasks, searchTasks
tasks.description: Create src/kanban/engine/queries.ts: Query API returning minimal data for agents. Each query loads only what's needed. getTask(id) returns single task. getReadyTasks() returns tasks with status!=done, not blocked, all deps done. getBlockedTasks() returns blocked tasks with reason. getTaskContext(id) returns task + parent + direct deps + dependents + tests + acceptance criteria + relevant decisions + recommended action. getDependencies(id) returns direct dependency tasks. getDependents(id) returns tasks depending on id. getChildren(id) returns child tasks. getParent(id) returns parent task. getTree(id) returns full subtree. getNextTasks() returns ready tasks sorted by priority. searchTasks(query) searches title/description.
acceptance_criteria: All query functions exist and return typed results
getTaskContext returns minimal operational context (< 2KB JSON)
getNextTasks sorts by priority: critical > high > medium > low
No query loads full kanban.json into agent context
notes: Core agent interface — must be token-efficient
Context size target: < 2000 chars for typical task

tasks.title: Tests for Query API
tasks.description: Tests for all query functions with various kanban states.
acceptance_criteria: getReadyTasks excludes blocked and done tasks

tasks.title: Context Builder — Progressive Context Levels
tasks.description: Create src/kanban/engine/context.ts: ContextBuilder with progressive levels. Level 1: task only. Level 2: task + parent + direct deps. Level 3: + dependents + tests. Level 4: + relevant decisions (from decisions.md). Level 5: + architecture.md sections. buildContext(taskId, level?) defaults to level 3. Returns JSON optimized for agent consumption. Includes recommended_action: 'start' | 'block' | 'wait' | 'complete' | 'split'.
acceptance_criteria: Level 1: ~200 chars, Level 3: ~1500 chars, Level 5: ~5000 chars
recommended_action logic: ready->start, blocked->block, in_progress->complete, has_children->split
Architecture sections filtered by module references

tasks.title: Research plan for implementing pattern system from nuevo-sastre kanban
tasks.description: Produce a comprehensive research plan that decomposes the pattern system implementation into manageable research subtasks. This task is RESEARCH AND PLANNING ONLY — it must NOT implement the pattern system, geometric engine, DSL, or SVG generator. CRITICAL FINDING: The repository source code contains ONLY the Kanban engine (13 TypeScript files under src/kanban/engine/ and src/cli/). The tasks in kanban.json marked as done (GEO-*, DSL-*, PAT-*, etc.) are administrative task definitions — their implementations do NOT exist in the source code. There is no geometry engine, no DSL, no pattern primitives, no SVG renderer, no validator. Everything must be built from scratch. The only reusable value is ~180 lines of generic infrastructure code (graph algorithms, atomic write pattern, NDJSON audit log). This research must determine: what patterns can be reused from the Kanban engine architecture, the complete geometric foundation, the domain model, the DSL architecture, and the first vertical slice.
evidence: Research plan complete. 6 subtasks executed: (1) Audit: repo has ONLY Kanban engine, ~180 lines reusable, (2) Geometry: mm-based, Y-up, 10 primitives, SVG direct mapping, (3) Domain model: 13 concepts, Pattern→Piece→Contour hierarchy, (4) DSL: hybrid declarative/imperative with pattern-native vocabulary, three-layer IR, (5) Vertical slice: A-line skirt front panel, 24 success criteria, (6) Synthesis: 18 decisions, 45 implementation tasks, 8 phases. All tasks completed. Validation passes.

tasks.title: Research: geometric foundation and SVG representation for pattern generation
tasks.description: Research the minimum geometric core needed to generate sewing patterns in SVG. Do NOT implement any geometry code. Analyze: coordinate system, units (mm/cm/inches), precision requirements, points, lines, segments, arcs, Bezier curves, paths, intersections, transformations, offsets, symmetries, SVG export, geometric validation. Evaluate the existing geometry engine (Point2D, Vector2D, Line, Arc, Bezier, Path, Polygon, Intersections, Offsets) for pattern-specific fitness. Deliverable: a technical proposal document specifying the minimum geometric foundation the first vertical slice needs, including which existing primitives suffice, which need extension, and which are missing entirely. ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA: (1) Coordinate system and unit strategy is proposed with justification; (2) Each geometric primitive is assessed for pattern-generation fitness; (3) SVG representation strategy is defined (direct coordinate mapping vs. transform-based); (4) Missing geometric capabilities are identified (e.g., parallel curves for seam allowance at non-straight segments, grading between sizes); (5) A clear recommendation for the first vertical slice's geometric requirements.
evidence: Geometric foundation research complete. Document produced: mm-based coordinate system, Y-up internally/Y-down at SVG, 10 primitives assessed (Point2D, Vector2D, Line, Ray, Segment, Arc, Bezier, Path, Circle, Polygon), 6 operation categories defined (intersections, transformations, offsets, projections, symmetries, distances), SVG representation strategy with direct coordinate mapping and mm units, minimum geometric core for first vertical slice identified (Point2D, Vector2D, Segment, Path, Polygon, translate/reflect, SVG renderer). Key finding: Bezier curves are THE critical curve type for armholes/necklines per industry standard.

tasks.title: Research: pattern domain model — semantic entities of garment patternmaking
tasks.description: Research what patternmaking concepts must be represented as semantic entities in the system BEFORE designing DSL syntax. Do NOT implement any model code. Analyze: body measurements, named points, lines, curves, contours, pieces, construction references, seam lines, allowances, notches, grainlines, darts, gathers, pleats, ease, transform operations, geometric relationships, parametric formulas. The research must answer: what concepts must the pattern system understand before DSL syntax is designed? Deliverable: a domain model proposal document with entity definitions, relationships, and the rationale for each entity's inclusion. ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA: (1) Every core patternmaking concept is identified and defined; (2) Relationships between entities are documented (e.g., a Piece contains Contours, Contours contain Curves); (3) Parametric dependency relationships are identified (e.g., bust width depends on bust measurement); (4) The model distinguishes between 'input' entities (measurements), 'construction' entities (intermediate geometry), and 'output' entities (final pieces); (5) Existing pattern primitives in the codebase (Piece, SeamAllowance, Notch, Grainline, Dart) are assessed for domain-model fitness.
evidence: Domain model proposal document produced: planning/domain-model-proposal.md. Covers all 5 acceptance criteria: (1) 13 core patternmaking concepts identified and defined with properties; (2) Entity relationships documented including containment hierarchy, reference relationships, and sewing relationships; (3) Parametric dependency graph with 3 layers (measurement, construction, cross-piece) identified; (4) Entity classification into input/construction/output entities; (5) Existing codebase (Piece, SeamAllowance, Notch, Grainline, Dart) assessed with gap analysis and recommendations. External research covers Valentina/Seamly2D, ASTM D6673/AAMA DXF, NIST STEP/EXPRESS model, and computational patternmaking literature.

tasks.title: Research: DSL architecture for AI-agent pattern communication
tasks.description: Research how an AI agent should communicate with the pattern system. Do NOT implement any DSL code. Analyze: syntax design, instruction structure, point references, measurements, geometric relationships, incremental construction, curves, dependencies between instructions, validation, error reporting, serialization, intermediate representation. Evaluate architectures like DSL→AST/IR→Parametric Geometry→SVG but do NOT assume this as final without justification. Assess the existing DSL (Lexer, Parser, Pratt expression parser, Interpreter, AST types) for pattern-specific fitness. Deliverable: a technical recommendation document for the DSL architecture and its relationship to the geometric engine. ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA: (1) At least 2 candidate architectures are evaluated with trade-offs; (2) The existing DSL's reusability for pattern instructions is assessed; (3) Intermediate representation strategy is recommended; (4) Error handling and validation approach is proposed; (5) The document specifies how the DSL relates to the domain model entities; (6) A clear recommendation with justification is provided.
evidence: DSL architecture research complete. Document produced recommending Hybrid DSL with pattern-native vocabulary (PIECE, DART, NOTCH, SEW). Three-layer IR: AST → PatternGraph (named entities + DAG) → Resolved Geometry → SVG. Key decisions: named references over indexed, automatic DAG dependency resolution, explicit units, Y-up coordinates, per-piece+per-edge seam allowance, declarative SEW relationships. Evaluated 3 architectures: declarative (Valentina-style), imperative (GarmentCode-style), hybrid (recommended). Existing parser infrastructure reusable; AST nodes must be pattern-specific.
